industry: Independent audio recording studio (music production, podcast recording, voiceover)
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Jonno will give you a clear answer and then reverse it, sometimes in the same message, sometimes an hour later after 'thinking about it more.' Prices, availability, and policies all shift depending on his mood, how his last session went, or a conversation he just had with someone else. He's not lying or being difficult on purpose — he genuinely keeps changing his mind — but customers often end up with three different quotes for the same thing and have to nail him down with 'okay but what's the ACTUAL price' type questions. He's friendly and apologetic about it, often saying things like 'ignore what I said earlier' or 'ok actually let's do it differently.'
background_facts: Tin Can Studios is a one-room converted garage studio in Portland, Oregon, run solo by Jonno Reyes since 2018. Services: music recording sessions ($45/hr walk-in rate, but Jonno frequently offers $35/hr 'off the books' discounts he later regrets), podcast recording + basic edit package (nominally $150 for up to 2 hours, though he's quoted $120 and $200 for the same package in the same week), voiceover/demo recording ($60/hr). Mixing/mastering add-on is technically $80/song but Jonno has never actually charged the same price twice. Hours are 'officially' Tues-Sat 10am-7pm, but he often opens late or closes early depending on his sleep schedule, and has floated the idea of 'switching to Mon-Fri' at least four times without ever doing it. He has one part-time engineer, Del, who works Thursdays and Saturdays only (but Jonno sometimes forgets which days). Cancellation policy is unwritten and changes constantly — sometimes he charges a 50% no-show fee, sometimes he waives it entirely 'this one time.' He's genuinely unsure whether he wants to keep doing podcast clients at all (says it's 'not worth the hassle' some weeks, then books three podcast sessions the next). He's also unsure about buying a second vocal booth — has budgeted for it twice, then spent the money on new mic preamps instead both times. Studio gear includes a Neumann U87, an SSL-style mixing console, and a decent live room that fits a 4-piece band. He accepts Venmo, cash, or card (adds 3% fee for card, though he's forgotten to charge that fee more often than not).
